MONDO:0007488.description: A progressive form of dementia characterized by the presence of protein deposits called Lewy bodies in the midbrain and cerebral cortex, and loss of cholinergic and dopaminergic neurons. The signs and symptoms overlap with Alzheimer and Parkinson disease.
MONDO:0007488.name: Lewy body dementia

MONDO:0008199.description: A Parkinson disease that begins after around the age of 50.
MONDO:0008199.name: late-onset Parkinson disease
synonym: Parkinson disease, age of onset, modifier, Multifactorial
Parkinson disease, late-onset, susceptibility to, Multifactorial

MONDO:0009265.description: Gaucher disease type 1 is the chronic non-neurological form of Gaucher disease (GD) characterized by organomegaly, bone involvement and cytopenia.
MONDO:0009265.name: Gaucher disease type I

MONDO:0009266.description: Gaucher disease type 2 is the acute neurological form of Gaucher disease (GD). It is characterized by early-onset and severe neurological involvement of the brainstem, associated with an organomegaly and generally leading to death before the age of 2.
MONDO:0009266.name: Gaucher disease type II

MONDO:0009267.description: Gaucher disease type 3 is the subacute neurological form of Gaucher disease (GD) characterized by progressive encephalopathy and associated with the systemic manifestations (organomegaly, bone involvement, cytopenia) of GD type 1.
MONDO:0009267.name: Gaucher disease type III
synonym: Gaucher disease, juvenile and adult, cerebral
cerebral juvenile and adult form of Gaucher disease

MONDO:0009268.description: Gaucher disease - ophthalmoplegia - cardiovascular calcification is a variant of Gaucher disease, also known as a Gaucher-like disease that is characterized by cardiac involvement.
MONDO:0009268.name: Gaucher disease-ophthalmoplegia-cardiovascular calcification syndrome

MONDO:0009699.description: Action myoclonus-renal failure syndrome (AMRF) is a rare epilepsy syndrome characterized by progressive myoclonus epilepsy in association with primary glomerular disease. Patients present with neurologic symptoms (including tremor, action myoclonus, tonic-clonic seizures, later ataxia and dysarthria) that may precede, occur simultaneously or be followed by renal manifestations including proteinuria that progresses to nephrotic syndrome and end-stage renal disease. In some patients, sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy, sensorineural hearing loss and dilated cardiomyopathy are associated symptoms.
MONDO:0009699.name: action myoclonus-renal failure syndrome
synonym: epilepsy, progressive myoclonic 4, with or without renal failure
epilepsy, progressive myoclonic, 4, with or without renal failure

MONDO:0009756.description: Niemann-Pick disease type A is a very severe subtype of Niemann-Pick disease, an autosomal recessive lysosomal disease, and is characterized clinically by onset in infancy or early childhood with failure to thrive, hepatosplenomegaly, and rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disorders.
MONDO:0009756.name: Niemann-Pick disease type A

MONDO:0011706.description: Kufor-Rakeb syndrome (KRS) is a rare genetic neurodegenerative disorder characterized by juvenile Parkinsonism, pyramidal degeneration (dystonia), supranuclear palsy, and cognitive impairment.
MONDO:0011706.name: Kufor-Rakeb syndrome
synonym: Pallidopyramidal degeneration with supranuclear upgaze paresis, and dementia

MONDO:0011871.description: Niemann-Pick disease type B is a mild subtype of Niemann-Pick disease, an autosomal recessive lysosomal disease, and is characterized clinically by onset in childhood with hepatosplenomegaly, growth retardation, and lung disorders such as infections and dyspnea
MONDO:0011871.name: Niemann-Pick disease type B

MONDO:0011945.description: Fetal Gaucher disease is the perinatal lethal form of Gaucher disease (GD).
MONDO:0011945.name: Gaucher disease perinatal lethal

MONDO:0012414.description: A rare condition that affects the nervous system. Signs and symptoms of the condition can develop any time from birth to adulthood and may include progressive dementia, seizures, lack of muscle coordination, and vision loss. CLN10-NCL is caused by changes (mutations) in the CTSD gene and is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner. Treatment options are limited to therapies that can help relieve some of the symptoms.
MONDO:0012414.name: neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis 10
synonym: neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis caused by mutation in CTSD
neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis due to cathepsin D deficiency

MONDO:0012517.description: Any Gaucher disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PSAP gene.
MONDO:0012517.name: Gaucher disease due to saposin C deficiency
synonym: Gaucher disease caused by mutation in PSAP
atypical Gaucher disease due to saposin C deficiency
atypical Gaucher's disease due to saposin c deficiency

MONDO:0012719.description: Encephalopathy due to prosaposin deficiency is a lysosomal storage disease belonging to the group of sphingolipidoses.
MONDO:0012719.name: combined PSAP deficiency

MONDO:0013737.description: A rare, complex type of hereditary spastic paraplegia characterized by an onset, in infancy or childhood, of the typical signs of spastic paraplegia (i.e. spastic gait and weakness of the lower limbs) associated with a variety of additional manifestations including upper limb spasticity and weakness, pseudobulbar dysarthria, bladder dysfunction, cerebellar ataxia, cataracts, and cognitive impairment that can progress to dementia. Brain imaging may show thinning of the corpus callosum and mild atrophy of the cerebrum and cerebellum. SPG46 is due to mutations in the GBA2 gene (9p13.2) encoding non-lysosomal glucosylceramidase.
MONDO:0013737.name: hereditary spastic paraplegia 46
synonym: GBA2 autosomal recessive complex spastic paraplegia
autosomal recessive complex spastic paraplegia caused by mutation in GBA2

MONDO:0018150.description: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder encompassing three main forms (types 1, 2 and 3), a fetal form and a variant with cardiac involvement (Gaucher disease - ophthalmoplegia - cardiovascular calcification or Gaucher-like disease).
MONDO:0018150.name: Gaucher disease
